title: Thoracic motion segment 6x6 stiffness matrix (average of T1-T2 to T11-T12), positive and negative loads
condition: intact, no preload, rib heads retained

quantity.name: 6x6 stiffness matrix (from inverted flexibility)
quantity.definition: Right-hand Cartesian system (Panjabi et al. 1974), fixed in space, origin at the centre of the UPPER vertebral body under no load; lower vertebra rigidly fixed. Fig 1: y axial (upward), z antero-posterior, x lateral; DOF 1-3 = translations along x, y, z; 4-6 = rotations about x (flexion-extension), y (axial rotation), z (lateral bending). Stiffness matrix obtained by INVERTING the measured 6x6 flexibility matrix (sagittal symmetry assumed: 12 non-zero coefficients). Values at 100 N force or 5 Nm moment; K+ from positive load components, K- from negative.

source.authors: Panjabi MM, Brand RA Jr, White AA III
source.n: 11 thoracic motion segments, one per level T1-T2 ... T11-T12, from 5 fresh cadaver spines
source.sample: fresh human cadaveric thoracic motion segments with intervening ligaments and rib heads/necks (ribs cut proximal to the transverse articulation)

protocol.summary: Load control, one load component at a time applied to the upper vertebra via a threaded rod through the vertebral body centre: forces 1 kp initial then increments of 3 kp up to 16 kp (~157 N); moments by 1 kp couples on 10 or 15 cm arms in 1 kp increments up to 6 kp; displacements read 4 min after each load (dial gauges, 3 steel balls); 100% humidity, 22 C; no preload.
how_to_simulate: Model a thoracic motion segment (two vertebrae, disc, ligaments, rib heads/necks only; no rib cage); fix the lower vertebra, reference point = centre of the upper vertebral body
Apply each of the 6 load components separately, positive and negative, without preload: forces up to 100 N, moments up to 5 Nm
Record all 6 displacements at 100 N / 5 Nm to build the 6x6 flexibility matrix, invert it to get the stiffness matrix (do NOT take reciprocals of flexibility terms)
Compare the 12 non-zero terms (converted to N/mm, N/deg, Nm/deg) with the level-averaged values
protocol.notes: Coordinate system: Right-hand Cartesian system (Panjabi et al. 1974), fixed in space, origin at the centre of the UPPER vertebral body under no load; lower vertebra rigidly fixed. Fig 1: y axial (upward), z antero-posterior, x lateral; DOF 1-3 = translations along x, y, z; 4-6 = rotations about x (flexion-extension), y (axial rotation), z (lateral bending). Stiffness matrix obtained by INVERTING the measured 6x6 flexibility matrix (sagittal symmetry assumed: 12 non-zero coefficients). Values at 100 N force or 5 Nm moment; K+ from positive load components, K- from negative. Per-level main and coupling flexibility coefficients are plotted in Figs 7-8 (not extracted; text: small variation along levels for main coefficients). No SD given. Specimens kept at 100% humidity (not immersed).

extraction.uncertainty: tabulated to 2-3 significant figures (x1e4); no SD
extraction.check_notes: All 24 stiffness values re-read from the rendered Table 1 image (pdftotext unusable). Cross-check: Edwards 1987 Table 3 quotes Panjabi K+ as Kyy 780 N/mm, Kzz 100, Ktt 152000 N·mm/rad, Kyz 50, consistent with K22, K33, K44, K23 here. Converted N/rad -> N/deg, N·mm/rad -> Nm/deg.

pass_rule.rule: diagonal terms within a factor 1.5 of the mean (no SD reported); off-diagonal sign and order of magnitude
